hook.content: Imagine you are a sound detective walking through a secret letter forest. Every tree and bush makes a special sound when the wind blows through it. Today, we are going to collect our favorite letter sounds in our sound basket so we can read and build brand new words like magic!

bigIdea.statement: Letters make specific sounds, and when we put those sounds together, we can read and write words.
bigIdea.whyItMatters: Knowing letter sounds is the superpower that unlocks all reading, helping you explore fun stories, write notes to friends, and read signs all around your world.

objectives.text: Produce the correct sounds for letters s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, and d when you hear or see them
Blend individual letter sounds together to read whole words

shouldKnow: Awareness that spoken words are made of separate sounds
Ability to listen carefully and repeat sounds

quickCheck.question: What sound does the letter 's' make at the beginning of the word 'sun'?
quickCheck.hint: Think about what a friendly snake says when it slithers!

Practice the special sounds for our core group of letters.
activities: Sorting sounds by mouth and tongue movements

roadmap.description: Put our sounds together like train cars to read real words.
activities: Reading mystery words with a partner

buildingFrom: Kindergarten phonemic awareness and single letter introduction
leadingTo: Writing simple sentences using phonetic spelling
realWorld: Reading favorite storybooks all by yourself
Writing birthday cards and grocery lists
Sounding out unfamiliar words on road signs and cereal boxes

mindset.encouragement: Some letter sounds can look or sound tricky, like 'c' and 'k', but your brain is growing stronger every time you practice. Take a deep breath and sound it out slowly!
mindset.growthTip: When you get stuck on a sound, trace the letter with your finger and say the sound out loud to help your brain remember.

curatorBrief.title: Letter Sounds & Word Blending Review
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome first-grade readers to a sound safari! Review the 13 foundational letter sounds (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d) and blend them together to read clear, decodable words.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Produce the correct sounds for letters s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, and d when you hear or see them

components.title: Letter Sound & Shape Match
components.intent: Review visual recognition and rapid discrimination for the target letters across Groups 1 and 2 (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d) using spoken prompts and form matching.

components.title: Say the Letter Sounds
components.intent: Engage in live spoken Direct Instruction to practice producing pure continuous sounds and onset associations for taught letters s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, and d.

components.title: Sound to Grapheme Challenge
components.intent: Identify confusable letters from spoken sounds and produce target letter sounds aloud across cumulative Groups 1 and 2.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Blend individual letter sounds together to read whole words

components.title: Sound-by-Sound Blending Station
components.intent: Demonstrate tapping individual phoneme tiles for words built purely from target letters (such as 'sat', 'pin', 'cat', 'red', 'ham') and blend them sequentially to form whole words.

components.title: Blend & Read CVC Words
components.intent: Practice direct instruction decodable word reading aloud with the live tutor, sounding out and reading CVC words composed of letters s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d.

components.title: CVC Word Workout & Picture Match
components.intent: Cold-decode printed words made from the target sounds, distinguish real words from nonsense words, and match decoded words to corresponding pictures.

finalAssessment.title: Cumulative Sound & Blending Check
finalAssessment.intent: Assess student mastery in both identifying letter sounds for s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d and blending those sounds to recognize and read complete decodable CVC words.

problems.question: What sound does the snake letter make?
problems.rationale: The letter S makes the /s/ sound like a hissing snake or the sun. The letter A makes /a/ and the letter T makes /t/.
problems.teachingNote: Have students trace the letter 's' in the air while making a continuous hissing sound.
successCriteria: Recall the primary sound for the consonant letter s.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.prompt: Match each letter to its sound cue.
problems.rationale: The letter p makes the /p/ sound in pig. The letter n makes the /n/ sound in nest, and the letter c makes the /k/ sound in cat.
problems.teachingNote: Remind students to say the first sound of each picture word out loud to match it to the correct letter.
successCriteria: Recall and identify the initial sound represented by the letter p.
Recall and identify the initial sound represented by the letter n.
Recall and identify the initial sound represented by the letter c.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word is made of the sounds /s/ /a/ /t/?
problems.rationale: The sounds /s/, /a/, and /t/ blend together smoothly to make the word sat. The other choices begin with different starting sounds, like /k/, /p/, and /m/.
problems.teachingNote: Guide students to use continuous blending by stretching the first sound into the vowel without pausing between phonemes.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes /s/, /a/, and /t/ to read the word sat.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.textWithBlanks: Dad will cook a fish in the [blank_1].
problems.rationale: The sentence describes cooking fish in a kitchen tool, and 'pan' is the correct decodable word using the target letter sounds. 'Pin' and 'pet' are incorrect distractors that share similar beginning sounds.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to sound out the entire word by blending the letter sounds /p/-/a/-/n/.
successCriteria: Read and decode simple three-letter words using targeted letter sounds
